metadata.methods_description: Participants performed 3-minute walking trials at five speeds (0.0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6 m/s) on a treadmill while viewing a static visual display through liquid crystal goggles that occluded vision for 1.5 seconds every 8–10 seconds. EEG was recorded from 120 scalp electrodes and 110 noise electrodes using 8 Brain Vision Amplifiers. Additional sensors included 8 EMG electrodes (bilateral sternocleidomastoid and trapezius), Loadsol insole sensors for gait events, and an APDM Opal IMU on the lower back. Walking speed order was randomized, with breaks offered between conditions. Participants were young adults (18–29 years) with normal or corrected vision and no history of musculoskeletal or neurological disorders.
